episodes.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
episodes.description: My guest today is Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, and we’re discussing the Anthropic IPO for our third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. So you’ll hear Hayden and I dive into this tension, and what to make of Anthropic’s unique corporate governance structure in the wake of the Jensen Huang saga. Read the full interview transcript on The Verge. episodes.title: The Professional Network Built for You and Your AI Agent
episodes.description: What if your AI agent could find the people you should know before you even start looking? Cosign is building a professional network around reputation and trusted recommendations, and now agents can use that network too. MTS host Sophia Dew sits down with a16z’s David Booth and Cosign’s Bella Nazzari to discuss what they’ve learned since launching Cosign, why traditional profiles often miss the operators doing the most important work, and how the Cosign Awards are surfacing talent through the people willing to vouch for them. They also explore an emerging behavior: people connecting their agents to Cosign to continuously find relevant people, lists, and opportunities, and what professional networking could look like when both humans and their agents participate. Resources: Follow David Boo

episodes.title: Rapid Response — Why everything is breaking: outages, AI, and the new cyber math, with CrowdStrike’s George Kurtz
episodes.description: Microsoft systems down. Air traffic systems down. Problems at Chase, United and Apple. After a week of outages across big systems, the AI conspiracy theories are in full swing. CrowdStrike founder and CEO George Kurtz joins Rapid Response to explain what’s actually going on. Kurtz describes how AI agents can turn a patch into a working exploit within an hour, why the old pyramid of hacktivists, criminals, and nation states has collapsed, and how CEOs are now taking services offline rather than risk being hacked. He also discusses CrowdStrike’s new AI Kill Switch, why slowing down the frontier labs won’t slow down the attackers, and what endurance racing has taught him about risk and speed. episodes.title: How AI Is Forcing China to Reshape Industrial Policy
episodes.description: Can Chinese tech companies help the country achieve technological self-reliance while keeping up in the AI arms race? On this episode, we speak with Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center and author of the High Capacity newsletter, about Beijing’s response to the global AI boom and the tensions between Chinese companies’ commercial ambitions and the government’s long-term plans. He explains how companies draw on shared expertise and supply chains to expand across industries including smartphones, robotics, EVs and semiconductors — and we also discuss Huawei’s efforts to compete with Nvidia and why technological success doesn’t necessarily translate into strong returns for stock investors in China. Read more: AI Threatens to Make China’s Jobs Slump
